title: Dispensing apparatus for use in a cued food delivery task
author: Deweese, Claiborne, et al.

steps.title: Assemble delivery receptacle
steps.instruction: Using three 12"×16" plywood pieces (⅕" thick), six Phillips‑head screws with washers, two 1" L‑brackets, a head‑entry detector, and a pellet receptacle, cut a 3"×3" square hole in the centre of a front‑panel piece, insert the pellet receptacle and loosely fasten with two screws, glue the photocells to the inside left and right sides of the receptacle, then tighten the screws. Glue the bottom of the head‑entry detector to the top of the pellet receptacle. Align each side panel lengthwise with the front panel, secure with Phillips screws, washers and two L‑brackets positioned ≈3¼" from the top and ≈3¼" from the bottom; repeat for the opposite side.

steps.title: Build Y‑connector tubing
steps.instruction: Gather one dual‑feed Y‑connector, two ¾"‑diameter clear PVC tubes (3" long), two ¾"‑diameter flexible PVC tubes (13" long), two 1"‑diameter PVC couplings (1½" long), two ¾"‑opening PVC 45° elbows, three ¾"‑diameter plain PVC end pipes (2" long), four ¾"‑diameter PVC female adapters (1¾" long), and one ¾"‑opening PVC 90° elbow. For Tube 1, connect in order: clear PVC tube → flexible PVC tube → 45° elbow → plain end pipe → female adapter → coupling → dual‑feed Y‑connector. Repeat the same sequence for Tube 2. Then attach the dual‑feed Y‑connector to a female adapter, connect that adapter to a plain end pipe, attach the plain pipe to the 90° elbow, and finally connect the elbow to the pellet receptacle.

steps.title: Construct deposit boxes
steps.instruction: Using two acrylic ballot boxes, two head‑entry detectors, four magnetic strips (1¾"×1"), and optional Phillips screws, for each box: (1) grind a ¾"×⅕" hole in the centre of the slot; (2) drill a ≈1"×⅕" hole in the back for detector wires; (3) place the head‑entry detector inside and feed its wire through the back hole; (4) glue a 1¾"×1" magnetic strip to the inside lid ≈1" from the slot; (5) glue the complementary magnetic strip to the bottom of the detector; (6) glue the detector’s white photo cells on either side of the slot hole on the underside of the top; optionally secure with screws.

steps.title: Wire deposit boxes to power and PC
steps.instruction: Using the black receptacle box (RB), a 28 V power‑supply box, two RCA Audio/Video cables (R1‑W1 and R2‑W2), DIS1, DIS2, and the deposit‑box boxes (B1 and B2), follow the connectivity diagram: **Deposit box 1 (B1)** – connect the detector output cable to Box 1 input; connect Box 1 TTL ground/output to the red RCA cable (R1) leading to PC1; connect Box 1’s 28 V port to the split 28 V cable from Box 2. **Deposit box 2 (B2)** – connect its detector output cable to Box 2 input; connect Box 2 TTL ground/output to the red RCA cable (R2) to PC1; split Box 2’s 28 V wire: one branch to Box 1’s 28 V port, the other to DIS1’s 28 V port. From the DIS2 28 V branch split again: one to DIS1’s 28 V input, the other to the black receptacle box (RB) 28 V input. **Receptacle box & power** – connect the detector output cable from the wooden delivery receptacle to RB input; connect RB’s 28 V input directly to the power‑supply box and to DIS2, completing the voltage circuit; connect TTL ground/output wires to Y2, which routes to PC1.

steps.title: Connect dispensers to DIS and PC
steps.instruction: With Cylinder 1 (C1) and Cylinder 2 (C2), DIS1, DIS2, two RCA connector cables, and PC1: **Cylinder 1** – attach the C1 cable to DIS1’s output port; connect the 28 V input on C1 to DIS2’s 28 V port; link DIS1’s TTL ground/input to the white RCA cable (W1) that runs to PC1. **Cylinder 2** – attach the C2 cable to DIS2’s output port; split the 28 V power as described in Step 4b3; connect DIS2’s TTL A/V input to the white RCA cable (W2) to PC1.

steps.title: Link dispensers to receptacle via Y‑connector
steps.instruction: Using the Y‑connector assembled in Step 2, connect the output of Cylinder 1 to the clear PVC tube of Tube 1, and similarly connect the clear PVC tube of Tube 2 to the output of Cylinder 2. Then attach the base of the fully assembled Y‑connector to the L‑shaped PVC connector inside the delivery receptacle.

description: In humans, studies investigating the relationship between brain responses to food-related stimuli and obesity typically present visual food cues without subsequent delivery of an edible food reward [1], [2], [3]. Here, we have developed a dispensing apparatus for use in a cued food-delivery task capable of delivering either a food reward (an M&M's® candy) or a non-food control item (e.g., plastic beads), while brain responses to pictorial cues are being recorded via the electroencephalogram (EEG). To build the apparatus, we used items from Med Associates, Inc. (St. Albans, VT, USA) and items available from regular hardware stores. What follows is a brief description of the laboratory setup and dispensing apparatus:•Two dispensers* hold either food rewards or non-food control items.•A computer in the laboratory control room (PC1) sends a signal via E-prime® software to display pictorial stimuli on a mirrored computer located in the participant recording room (PC2).•PC1 simultaneously sends a signal via E-prime® software to one of two dispensers (C1, C2) to dispense either a food or non-food control item.•A plastic tube directs the food reward/non-food item via a Y-connector from C1/C2 to a metal tray housed in a dispensing receptacle.•A photo cell is attached to the metal tray to detect when the item is picked up by the participant; the timestamp is recorded by PC1.•Two deposit boxes are equipped with photo cells to detect when the food reward or non-food item is deposited by the participant; the timestamp is recorded by PC1.•During the task, the participant's brain responses are being recorded via dense-array EEG, which is monitored on a Macintosh computer in the laboratory control room. * The dispensers used to deliver food rewards and non-food control items are pre-assembled dispensers and require no additional modification or assembly; product information may be found in the “Supply list” section.
